basics.name: Aidan McLean
basics.label: Full-Stack Developer
status: Research Assistant @ McMaster Faculty of Engineering
basics.lede: I am a Full-Stack Developer, and I enjoy designing and developing solutions based on real needs. My most recent projects are a research platform at McMaster where researchers benchmark AI battery models, and a full-stack e-commerce platform for an independent record label.
basics.contactNote: Open to hearing about software development & IT work. The fastest way to reach me is email.

highlights: Launched a custom e-commerce platform in October 2026, designed and built solo, giving the label its own storefront and staff admin for selling merchandise both online and in person.
Took 10 orders on launch day across a catalogue of 21 products and 18 artists, through a reliable Stripe checkout with accurate inventory tracking.
Built dual-currency payment processing in CAD and USD, with calculated shipping rates and local pickup options in Ontario and Connecticut.

Secured staff access with role-based permissions, two-factor sign-in, and an audit trail of every change to money and inventory, with automated testing, deployments, and error monitoring in production.

Established the label's professional presence on its own domain with branded business and customer email, and kept its online store running for 18 months without an outage, including the move to the new platform with no interruption to sales.

Developed a full-stack benchmarking platform for battery State-of-Charge estimation algorithms, where submitted models are evaluated in isolated Docker containers and ranked across 18+ performance metrics.

Translated requirements from weekly planning meetings and a prioritized issue backlog into delivered fixes and features across the REST API, PostgreSQL schema, and React interface, keeping development aligned with the research group's needs.

Built administrative tooling that let the research group manage users and submissions independently, including account bans, session revocation, private model visibility, and submission on a researcher's behalf.
Redesigned the platform's interface with shadcn/ui, added downloads for models and evaluation results, and implemented in-app and email notifications for submission and evaluation status.
Managed the platform's pre-production environment on Compute Canada's OpenStack cloud, including NGINX configuration, PM2 process management, and SSL/TLS certificate renewal.
Customized Drupal Webforms with JavaScript to implement dynamic form behaviour, validation, and improved user experience.
Built front-end integrations with Microsoft APIM to apply business logic, route requests securely, and connect forms to backend services.
Developed a TypeScript front-end application that integrated with an internal GIS map server to retrieve and visualize location-based data.
Picked up Drupal, APIM, and Power Automate on the job and put them straight to use on live production forms.
Documented APIs, workflows, and form logic so other developers could pick up the work without re-deriving it.

projects.name: Independent Record Label E-Commerce Platform
projects.summary: A full-stack e-commerce platform built solo for an independent record label: two Next.js 16 App Router applications in a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo, sharing a Drizzle ORM data layer over Postgres, better-auth authentication, and a Base UI component library.
projects.detail: Pricing, checkout, refunds, and stock logic live in the shared data package, so both applications run the same unit-tested code. In production since October 2026, handling real orders and payments online and in person.
highlights: Built a Stripe Checkout flow that reprices every line server-side and reserves stock in a single transaction with deterministically ordered row locks, with signature-verified, idempotent webhooks and a 15-minute reconciliation job that recovers paid sessions whose webhook never arrived.

Implemented USD and CAD pricing with no FX conversion, rendering both prices in React Server Components and selecting one with a pre-paint inline script, so product pages keep static generation with ISR and avoid layout shift.

Enforced permission-level RBAC with better-auth's access-control plugin on every admin route and server action, with invite-only accounts, TOTP two-factor sign-in, and an append-only audit log enforced by Postgres triggers.

Validated every server action with Zod, implemented rate limits as atomic Postgres upserts that hold across serverless instances, stored only salted hashes of visitor IPs, and scrubbed personal data from Sentry error reports before they leave the server or browser.

Deployed as two Vercel projects on Neon Postgres, with a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs typecheck, lint, 142 Vitest tests, and build against a real Postgres instance, applies migrations on merge, and runs scheduled jobs for reconciliation and staff alerts.

projects.name: SoC Model Benchmarking Platform
projects.summary: A research platform where battery researchers upload State-of-Charge estimation models and have them scored and ranked on 18+ metrics: a TypeScript Express REST API and React client over PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM, better-auth authentication, and a Python scoring tool run in Docker.
projects.detail: Designed and built as a four-person capstone project, writing most of the Express backend and much of the React client, then developed further as a research assistant at McMaster. The lab has since rebuilt the platform on a new codebase.
highlights: Built an asynchronous evaluation pipeline that runs each submission in its own short-lived Docker container with a read-only filesystem and 2 GB memory, 2 CPU, and 100-process limits, parses the scorer's JSON output, and moves each model through pending, processing, ready, and error states.

Secured model uploads with Multer type and size limits, per-user storage paths, filename sanitization against path traversal, and inspection of every zip entry, rejecting nested archives and disallowed file types before anything reaches the evaluator.

Implemented authentication on better-auth with its admin, username, and bearer plugins, requiring email verification and a strong password policy, limiting sign-in attempts to 5 a minute, and enforcing roles, bans, and ownership-gated access to submissions through Express middleware.

Built admin tools to ban users and revoke their sessions, with the session cookie cache shortened to 20 seconds so revocations take effect almost immediately, and delivered results by email and live in-app notifications over Server-Sent Events.
Added structured Winston logging with daily-rotated error logs, and deployed the platform on Compute Canada's OpenStack cloud with Docker Compose, NGINX, PM2, and SSL/TLS.
